headline_marked: Biman to [[buy 10 Airbus planes]] to expand fleet
headline: Biman to buy 10 Airbus planes to expand fleet
summary: The government is negotiating a purchase of four A350-900 wide-body and six A321neo narrow-body aircraft to build a sustainable mixed fleet.
details: Biman Bangladesh Airlines is negotiating to purchase 10 Airbus aircraft to expand the national carrier's share of the air travel market. The proposed purchase includes four A350-900 wide-body aircraft and six A321neo narrow-body jets.

This move follows a recent agreement with Boeing to purchase 25 aircraft, including 15 wide-body and 10 narrow-body planes. The first Boeing aircraft is expected to be delivered between 2027-28 and the last by 2035.
Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat stated that the number of aircraft was determined based on Biman's network planning, range, and projected passenger numbers.
The wide-body aircraft will be used for high-demand Middle Eastern routes and long-haul services to Europe and North America, while narrow-body planes will serve regional and short-haul routes.
Minister Millat explained that the government is following the 'Ethiopian Airlines model' to grow the fleet from its current 19 aircraft to a much larger scale.
Currently, Biman carries only about 20 percent of total passenger demand, while foreign airlines serve the remaining 80 percent. The new aircraft are intended to address this fleet shortage.
The purchases will be funded by Biman's own earnings and through suitable financing arrangements, meaning there will be no direct pressure on the national budget.

headline: 6 deaths in 24 hours: Dengue death toll hits 239 this year
summary: Nearly 2,000 people were admitted to hospitals across Bangladesh in a single day as the dengue outbreak continues.
details: Six people died from dengue fever in the last 24 hours across Bangladesh, according to the Health Emergency Operation Center and Control Room of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
In the same period, 1,942 people were admitted to hospitals nationwide for dengue treatment.
The DGHS report indicates that the highest number of admissions were in the Dhaka division (outside the city corporations), with 378 patients, followed by Chittagong division with 301 patients.
Other admissions include 229 in Dhaka South City Corporation, 178 in Dhaka North City Corporation, 264 in Khulna, 213 in Barishal, 197 in Rajshahi, 120 in Mymensingh, 56 in Rangpur, and 6 in Sylhet.
The total number of deaths attributed to dengue this year has now reached 239.
A total of 77,672 people have been admitted to hospitals for dengue treatment so far this year, with 72,008 patients having been discharged.
The health authorities continue to monitor the situation as hospital admissions remain high across all divisions of the country.
